reason: Both conversations reach the right diagnosis (snapped drive belt) and avoid naming an unsupported part number. Conversation 2 ends better: it supports the DIY repair the customer is willing to do, says to search 'Hotpoint TVHM8 drive belt' or confirm the full model, mentions the tensioner/idler wheel, and keeps the engineer as an option. Conversation 1 gives clearer early panel-removal steps, but then over-escalates by telling a screwdriver-equipped customer to call an engineer for a standard belt job. Conversation 2 has flaws: confusing wording ('that is your fault'), an inconsistent claim that panel removal 'requires an engineer', and repeated unplug reminders. These are minor next to its more useful final advice.
